# Parley v0.1.69

This unnotarized test beta adds a configuration backup to Settings, regroups
Settings so every control saves as it changes, reports a configuration file
Parley cannot read instead of quietly replacing it, and makes every Settings
section reachable from the command palette. Nothing changes in the agent
protocol (still 34).

## Export and restore your configuration

**Settings > General > Backup** writes this runtime's configuration to one
JSON file: workspaces with their panes as stopped templates (vendor, name,
role, lead, folder and the remembered profile choice), groups and pins, split
and saved layouts, custom permission profiles and default profile choices,
recipes, favourite folders, worktree repositories, and the terminal,
appearance, voice, notification and update preferences. It is built from
allowlisted values, never a copy of Application Support. The private things in
it are names, folder paths, recipe instructions and the names and summaries of
custom profiles.

Never in the file: relay credentials, control tokens, tickets, handoff and
activity history, context captures and returned files, container daemon and
container ids, worktree receipts, command-run trust, team grants, launch
generations, the session-only command-run switches, first-run and trust
confirmations, and the recent-folder history. A store that could not be read
at launch is left out and named rather than exported as defaults.

**Restore Configuration…** shows a preview before anything changes: which
workspaces it replaces and with what, the counts, every setting that changes
(the SwiftPM compatibility opt-in first), profile changes, the automation
policies, templates that ran in a container, folders this Mac does not have,
what the export left out, the retention change, and anything still live.
Replace needs a quiet Parley: every agent stopped and every shell closed, no
launch review open, no Ask waiting, no delegation, command run or team
session active, no container being prepared and no dictation running. Parley
lists the blockers and never stops anything because Restore was chosen.

Replace puts the whole exported configuration in place of the current one,
with fresh workspace and pane identities; it is not a merge. The stores and
preferences are written first with their exact previous bytes kept and a
journal on disk, then the workbench in one saved change, then the split
layouts. A failure before the workbench is replaced puts every store back
exactly; a crash part-way is recovered at the next launch, which says what it
did. Every restored pane is stopped and nothing launches; no saved approval
becomes execution authority; missing folders are kept as written and shown as
MISSING; a lower history retention is asked about separately. A Production
export is restored only into Production and a Development export only into
Development.

## Settings: Appearance holds how a pane looks, Terminal how it behaves

**Settings > Appearance** is now one grouped, flexible form: the shared font,
the imported Ghostty appearance, and the Ghostty options about how a pane
looks (theme and colours, font rendering, background and padding), with
**Restore Parley Defaults** for the whole tab. **Settings > Terminal** keeps the
terminal type and the options about how a pane behaves (cursor, scrollback,
mouse and clipboard, shell integration), with its own **Restore Ghostty
Defaults**. The font controls apply as they change like every other Settings
control; the Apply and Cancel buttons are gone. The theme pickers are disabled
while an imported appearance supplies the colours and offer **Remove Imported
Appearance**. Every section header says when a change reaches a pane: current
and new panes, new panes, or new shells. A value Ghostty refuses is reported
beside the section you changed.

## Settings: General, retention and the palette

**Settings > General** lists Software updates, Swift package builds, a new
**Local history** section (the retention choice, the same as Status Center >
History, and **Manage History…**), **Configuration**, **Backup**, and the two
session-only command-run switches last under a *This session only* header.
Every Settings section is a command in the palette (Command-K): type
*settings*, or a word such as *scrollback* or *notifications*.

## A configuration file Parley cannot read

When a configuration store cannot be read at launch (workspace split layouts,
saved layouts, recipes, custom permission profiles, favourite folders, the
terminal font, the imported Ghostty appearance or the Ghostty options),
Parley runs on defaults for that store only, says so in **Settings > General >
Configuration** and **Status Center > Health** with the reason and the
fallback, and keeps the unreadable bytes beside the store (a
`.unreadable-<time>` copy, or a `.unreadable` preference) instead of deleting
or writing over them. **Reveal in Finder** shows the file. An unreadable saved
layouts file no longer stops the terminal stack from starting, and a damaged
favourites value is no longer overwritten by the next save. Help has a
troubleshooting section for it.

## Going back to v0.1.68

Saved data is unchanged: v0.1.68 reads the same workspaces, layouts, profiles,
recipes and preferences. An exported configuration file is new and v0.1.68
cannot read one. A `configuration-restore.json` left by an interrupted restore
is ignored by v0.1.68.

## Validation and known limits

The release workflow repeats the following before publishing this beta:
- the deterministic checks and the repository scans;
- the app build and the 25-round Ghostty soak;
- packaging, checksums and packaged-launch verification.

Checked before the pull requests merged: 623 native checks, 82 script tests,
both scans, the build and the 25-round soak in a Command Line Tools Tart VM,
and the checks on GitHub's Xcode 26.6 runner. The backup went through two
independent Codex reviews; every finding was applied or recorded. Not yet
checked by hand in the app: the new Settings forms and the backup round trip
(docs/test-scenarios.md P1.8, P2.11, P2.12, P3.8). Two limits are recorded
rather than fixed: a restore holds no mutation reservation beyond re-reading
the coordinators at Replace, and a template that ran in a container comes
back as a host template with a disclosure.

Agy's loading of Parley's instructions from its added folder is still
unverified, fresh or resumed.

This is an ad-hoc-signed, unnotarized test beta. It does not update the
stable Sparkle feed or Homebrew cask. Follow the included installation
instructions.
